findings.text: The task can't be picked up from its folder: task `o25d5dte` in `../session.jsonl:13` still says `"state":"queued"`. Nothing marks it started, links it to `errors/`, or records the branch or commit `b332e4ea7`. The only link is a free-text log line at `../session.jsonl:66`. Set the task's state and `dir`, and close it with an outcome once the branch merges.

No test covers the wiring the "Done when" depends on. `Servex/ErrorLine.test.mjs` calls `ErrorLine.note()` directly, so nothing proves that a throwing tool behind `server()` (`Servex/agents/tools.js:614`) or `MCP.call()` (`Servex/MCP.js:106`) writes exactly one line and still returns `isError`. A three-line test would prove it: `server()` with a stub tool that throws, then read the last line.

Every thrown tool error now writes a line, including the agent's own mistakes (bad arguments, "no such path"), so a busy agent's `session.jsonl` may collect many `"error"` lines that are not bugs. Watch the volume after the restart before also adding non-tool catch sites.

The new line comes from `SpawnLog.note`, so it carries `ts` (`Servex/SpawnLog.js:52`), while the pid lines from `SpawnLog.put` carry `at`. The contract in indexing-past-work §6 says "`by` and `ts`", so the new line is the one that follows it; the pid lines are the ones that differ.

It meets the brief. The line puts `error` as its first key, followed by `where`, `tool` and `agent` (`Servex/ErrorLine.js:28`). The tool still returns its error result. `note()` is wrapped in try/catch and its write is async with `.catch`, so a failed write can't add a second error. `MCP` is assign-based (`initialize()`), so the `on_error` option set in `Servex/Servex.js:148` reaches `this.on_error`. I ran `node Servex/ErrorLine.test.mjs` in the worktree: ok.

The docs are up to date. `Servex/readme.md` lists `ErrorLine.js` and its test, `doc/tool-process.md` "If a tool throws" describes the line, and the indexing-past-work §5 row changed from "planned" to "works … from the first Servex restart". The `errors` log fits the readme's existing `logs/<name>.jsonl` pattern. I found nothing new left unlisted.
